Project for Concept project

Glowyn: content system for a skincare launch

Content system design · 2025

No metrics. Concept work only.

Scope of work

  • Five content pillars mapped to stages of buyer awareness
  • Nine-post launch grid planned as one continuous composition
  • Caption voice guide with worked examples
  • Ingredient education series written for a non-expert reader

My tools

  • Canva
  • Notion

A self-directed brief. Skin care brand with no following, no content history, and a launch in 30 days. I built the pillar structure, the grid rhythm, and the caption voice from zero. There is no client, no live account, and no growth to report. The planning work is real; the numbers are not claimed.

Frames

Why this exists

I wanted a skincare brief that was narrow enough to be honest about. Building a system for a brand with no audience forces every decision to be explicit: what does the first post say, what does the grid look like before anyone follows it, and why would a stranger stop scrolling.

This is a concept project. There is no client, no live account, and no growth to report. What is real is the planning work below.

The pillar structure

Five pillars, each tied to how far the reader is from buying.

  • Education. How an ingredient actually works, written plainly.
  • Routine. Where a product sits in an existing morning or night order.
  • Proof. Texture, consistency, wear time. Things you can see.
  • Objection. The reasons someone does not buy, answered instead of ignored.
  • Brand. Who makes it and why it exists.

The grid alternates heavy education posts with light product posts so the feed does not read as a catalogue.

Voice

Plain language, short sentences, no clinical claims. A caption can explain niacinamide without sounding like a leaflet. The guide includes before-and-after rewrites so the tone survives a change of writer.

What I would test first

Which pillar earns saves rather than likes. Saves are the honest signal for education content, and they decide what the second month leans on.
